content: Naive full-file CSV load into a DataFrame can use 3-4x the file's on-disk size in RAM once dtypes are inferred and Python object columns materialize (a 5GB CSV can require 15-20GB RAM), which crashes on typical dev/laptop machines. pandas.read_csv(chunksize=N) returns an iterator that keeps RSS memory flat across arbitrarily large files; pick chunksize by rows (start ~100k) balanced against column count/dtype width, and specify dtype=/usecols= explicitly to reduce inference cost and skip unneeded columns. Accumulating output rows in a plain Python list across chunks before writing defeats the purpose -- flush/write incrementally per chunk instead.
